skill.name: linear
skill.description: Use the Linear CLI to manage issues, projects, teams, comments, links, attachments, and GraphQL workflows from an AI coding session.
skill.summary: Manage Linear issues, projects, comments, links, attachments, and GraphQL workflows through guided CLI commands.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: The skill is documentation for a Linear CLI integration, and many static hits are Markdown examples rather than executable code. Confirmed risks include global package installation, broad Linear mutation commands with --yes, raw GraphQL access, possible credential exposure through config or external headers, a prompt-injection style QA prompt, and an overbroad /tmp cleanup example.

remediation.issue: QA prompt contains direct agent-control instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Move QA instructions outside the published skill package or label them as untrusted test material that must not override system or marketplace review instructions.
Replace the command with redacted CLI output such as linear auth show --redacted, and warn users never to paste raw config contents into chat.
Require the agent to summarize planned mutations and get explicit user approval immediately before using --yes.

remediation.issue: Upload responses and attachment downloads use predictable /tmp paths.
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp-created directories, restrict file permissions, and delete only named files created by the workflow.
Replace the glob with exact paths created during the test, such as /tmp/linear-qa-test.txt and /tmp/downloaded.txt.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting asks users to add an API key header in a browser-based explorer.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer local CLI validation or clearly warn users not to enter production API keys into third-party web tools.

Interacts with Linear for issue tracking and project management using the `linear` command.
- Use for Linear issue/project/teams management via the CLI or GraphQL (`linear gql`).
- Defaults: `linear config set default_team_id TEAM_KEY`, `linear config set default_output json|tab
- Inspect or reset defaults: `linear config show`, `linear config unset default_output`
- **Branches**: Name as `{TICKET}-{short-name}` (e.g., `ENG-123-fix-auth`); prefer git worktrees for
- **Assignment**: Assign yourself when starting work (`linear issue update ENG-123 --assignee me --y
- **Sub-issues**: Set parent to associate related work (requires UUID: `linear issue update ENG-123
- **Scope creep**: Create separate issues for discovered work; link with blocks relation (`linear is
| `linear issues list` | List issues with filters |
| `linear issue view ID` | View single issue |
| `linear issue update ID` | Update issue (assign, state, priority, parent*) |
| `linear issue link ID` | Link issues (blocks, related, duplicate) |
| `linear issue comment ID` | Add comment to issue |
| `linear issue delete ID` | Archive an issue |
| `linear project view ID` | View project details |
| `linear project update ID` | Update project (state, name, dates) |
| `linear project delete ID` | Archive a project |
| `linear project add-issue` | Add issue to project |
| `linear project remove-issue` | Remove issue from project |
*`--parent` requires UUIDs, not identifiers. See [Finding IDs](#finding-ids).
- `--team ID\|KEY` - Specify team (required for most commands)
**Note:** `--parent` requires UUIDs. Get UUID with `linear issue view ID --json | jq -r '.issue.id'`
- [ ] List teams to get TEAM_KEY: `linear teams list`
- [ ] Create parent issue: `linear issue create --team KEY --title "Epic" --yes`
- [ ] Create child issue: `linear issue create --team KEY --title "Task" --yes`
- [ ] Get parent UUID: `linear issue view PARENT_ID --json | jq -r '.issue.id'`
- [ ] Set parent (UUID required): `linear issue update CHILD_ID --parent PARENT_UUID --yes`
- [ ] Create another issue to link: `linear issue create --team KEY --title "Blocked" --yes`
- [ ] Link blocking issue: `linear issue link ISSUE_ID --blocks OTHER_ID --yes`

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: QA.md contains agent-control language such as "STOP. DO NOT RUN ANY COMMANDS YET" and instructs the agent not to read skill files directly. This can redirect an AI reviewer or user agent away from its governing instructions if the file is treated as trusted.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The suspicious language directly addresses an AI agent and attempts to control tool order and file-reading behavior. The context is QA documentation, so confidence is high but not absolute malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Overbroad Temporary File Cleanup
semantic_findings.description: The QA cleanup step removes /tmp/*.txt in addition to the named test file. An agent following this literally can delete unrelated temporary text files owned by the user.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The command uses a broad glob in /tmp and the file shows it as a cleanup instruction. This is a concrete destructive side effect beyond a single test artifact.

content.user_title: Manage Linear Issues from Your AI Agent
content.value_statement: Project updates stall when issues, links, comments, and project records are spread across Linear. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through safe Linear CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Lists, searches, and views Linear issues with team, assignee, state, and JSON output options.
Creates, updates, comments on, links, and archives Linear issues when the user approves mutations.
Lists, creates, updates, deletes, and associates Linear projects with issues.
Documents GraphQL recipes for attachments, comments, parent issues, relations, assignments, and ID lookup.
Explains authentication, configuration, attachment downloads, and common troubleshooting flows.
limitations: Requires the external linear CLI to be installed and available on PATH.
Requires a valid Linear API key or existing Linear CLI authentication.
Commands with --yes can change or archive workspace records, so users should approve mutations first.
Raw GraphQL recipes require correct UUIDs, schema knowledge, and careful handling of upload URLs.

use_cases.title: Daily Issue Review
use_cases.description: Review assigned Linear issues, inspect details, and collect UUIDs for follow-up work.

use_cases.title: Project Coordination
use_cases.description: Create related tasks, link blockers, update project state, and add implementation comments.

use_cases.title: Linear API Workflows
use_cases.description: Use documented GraphQL recipes for attachments, file uploads, relations, assignments, and workspace lookup.

prompt_templates.title: Show My Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Linear skill to list my active issues for team TEAM_KEY. Show identifiers, titles, states, and links.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Linear issue for this bug in team TEAM_KEY. Draft the title and description first, then ask before running any mutation.

prompt_templates.title: Link Related Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the UUIDs for ENG-123 and ENG-456, then prepare a command to mark ENG-123 as blocking ENG-456. Ask before using --yes.

prompt_templates.title: Attach Evidence with GraphQL
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GraphQL recipes to upload a file and attach it to ENG-123. Keep signed URLs and API keys out of the final response.

output_examples.input: List my current Linear issues for the platform team.
output: Found three active issues assigned to you in the platform team.
Each result includes the issue identifier, title, state, assignee, priority, and Linear URL.
Completed and canceled issues were excluded by the default state filter.

output_examples.input: Create a bug task and link it to the parent epic.
output: Prepared a new bug issue with a concise title, reproduction notes, and acceptance criteria.
Identified the parent issue UUID because Linear requires UUIDs for parent relationships.
Requested confirmation before creating the issue and applying the parent link.

output_examples.input: Help me attach a screenshot to an issue.
output: Requested an upload URL through Linear GraphQL, then used the returned upload instructions.
Created an attachment using the asset URL after upload completion.
Did not print API keys, signed upload headers, or private attachment URLs in the final message.

best_practices: Confirm every command that creates, updates, links, comments on, or archives Linear records.
Use identifiers for normal issue commands and UUIDs when Linear requires parent or GraphQL IDs.
Keep API keys, config file contents, signed upload URLs, and attachment data out of chat output.
anti_patterns: Running mutation commands with --yes before the user reviews the planned change.
Printing ~/.config/linear/config.json or raw authentication headers into the conversation.
Using broad cleanup commands such as rm /tmp/*.txt after attachment tests.

faq.question: What tools does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires the linear CLI, a valid Linear account, and either configured CLI auth or a Linear API key.

faq.question: Can it create or delete Linear issues?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation covers issue creation, updates, comments, links, and archive operations. Users should approve each mutation first.

faq.question: Does it support Linear projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents project listing, viewing, creation, updates, deletion, and adding or removing issues from projects.

faq.question: When should I use GraphQL recipes?
faq.answer: Use GraphQL only when built-in CLI commands do not cover the operation, such as specific attachment or relation workflows.

faq.question: How does it handle attachments?
faq.answer: It documents authenticated downloads, issue attachment directories, and a three-step upload flow using signed URLs.

faq.question: What security care is needed?
faq.answer: Avoid exposing API keys, config files, signed upload URLs, and private issue data. Confirm all workspace mutations before execution.
